blindSummary:
This state/province was swept into the same fight over student human-rights protections that engulfed the capital, but with the institutions on opposite sides: on 24 April 2024 the state/province legislature passed a bill to repeal the student human-rights ordinance in force here since 10 July 2020 (its non-discrimination clause covers gender identity and sexual orientation), and the state/province education office sued to overturn the repeal, obtaining a suspension of the repeal's execution from the national supreme court on 30 May 2024, so the ordinance remains in effect. On 21 February 2025 this state/province's and the capital's education offices filed a joint response to a communication from three UN human-rights experts, appearing as "stakeholders (enforcing authorities)" in the repeal dispute still pending before the supreme court and opposing the rollback on constitutional and treaty grounds.

The dispute runs through student non-discrimination rules. No traveler-facing enforcement action, arrest, or event obstruction is documented for this state/province, and no other incident or enforcement series was identified.

This state/province's section records: the provincial legislature passed a repeal bill on 24 April 2024 against the ordinance enacted 10 July 2020 (its non-discrimination clause covers gender identity and sexual orientation); the education office challenged the repeal before the supreme court on 13 May 2024 and obtained suspension of its execution on 30 May 2024, so the ordinance remains in effect; it argues the repeal violates the constitution and international human-rights treaties. The capital's section records its 11 July 2024 petition against the capital city council's abolition and the supreme court's 23 July 2024 suspension.
